variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
integer :: x = 10
real(8), parameter :: pi_val = 3.141592653589793d0
! Variables must be declared before executable statements
variables.notes: `::` is standard in modern free-form Fortran. `parameter` indicates a constant.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
integer :: i = 42
real :: r = 3.14
real(kind=8) :: dp = 3.14d0  ! Double precision
complex :: c = (1.0, 2.0)
logical :: b = .true.
character(len=20) :: str = "string"
data_types.notes: `kind` parameters define the precision of numeric types.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
! Arithmetic
res = 2 + 3 * 4
pow = 2 ** 10

! Relational (new / old forms)
if (x == y .or. a .eq. b) then
! Logical: .not., .and., .or.
operators.notes: Modern Fortran supports both `==`, `>`, etc., and the older `.eq.`, `.gt.` syntax.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if (x > 0) then
    print *, "Positive"
else if (x < 0) then
    print *, "Negative"
else
    print *, "Zero"
end if

for_loop.title: For Loop (Do Loop)
for_loop.code:
integer :: i
do i = 1, 10
    print *, i**2
end do

! Implied do-loop in array constructor
squares = [ (i**2, i=1, 10) ]
for_loop.notes: The `do` loop is Fortran's equivalent of a for-loop. Array constructors often use implied do-loops.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
integer :: count = 0
do while (count < 5)
    print *, count
    count = count + 1
end do
while_loop.notes: `do while` loops execute as long as the logical expression is true.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
function calc_mean(arr, n) result(res)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real, intent(in) :: arr(n)
    real :: res
    
    if (n == 0) then
        res = 0.0
    else
        res = sum(arr) / n
    end if
end function calc_mean
functions.notes: Functions return a value defined by `result`. `intent(in)` specifies read-only arguments for safety.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
real, dimension(3) :: vec = [1.5, 2.3, 4.1]
real :: mat(2,3) ! 2 rows, 3 cols

! Whole array operations are native
mat = mat * 2.0

! Accessing (1-based indexing default)
val = mat(1, 2)
arrays.notes: Fortran has powerful native multidimensional arrays (column-major). Indexing is 1-based by default.

maps.title: Derived Types (Structs)
maps.code:
type :: key_value
    character(len=10) :: key
    integer :: value
end type key_value

type(key_value), dimension(2) :: map
map(1) = key_value("a", 1)

val = map(1)%value
maps.notes: Fortran lacks native hash maps. Derived types (structs) accessed with `%` are used to build such structures.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
integer :: ios
real, allocatable :: arr(:)

! IO error handling via iostat
open(unit=10, file="data.txt", iostat=ios)
if (ios /= 0) print *, "Error opening file"

! Allocation error handling via stat
allocate(arr(100), stat=ios)
if (ios /= 0) print *, "Out of memory"
error_handling.notes: Error handling typically relies on checking status variables (`iostat`, `stat`) returned by operations.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in Fortran
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: Fortran uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: Fortran is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: Fortran provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: Fortran converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: Fortran treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Fortran formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: Fortran executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: Fortran indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: Fortran emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in Fortran
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: Fortran uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: Fortran stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: Fortran uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: Fortran provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: Fortran loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
